record.notes: Royal Assent 25 November 2024 (S.O. 2024, c. 24). Order in Council 361/2025, approved on 28 January 2025, named 29 January 2025 as the day Schedule 1, ss. 1-16 (the Enhancing Digital Security and Trust Act, 2024) came into force, together with part of Schedule 2 (amendments to the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act); the rest of Schedule 2 came into force on 1 July 2025. Schedule 1 has not been amended. The AI duties in ss. 5 and 6 apply only to public-sector entities and circumstances prescribed by regulation. As of the e-Laws currency date of 9 October 2026 the only regulations under the Act are O. Reg. 51/26 (cyber security) and O. Reg. 52/26 (digital technology affecting individuals under 18), which took effect on 1 July 2026, so no regulation under s. 7 yet prescribes entities for the AI provisions. Section 12 provides that the Act creates no private law duty of care. Ontario's Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Directive separately governs AI use by ministries and provincial agencies.

judgment.status_reasoning: Schedule 1, s. 17 brings the Act in Schedule 1 into force on a day named by proclamation. Order in Council 361/2025 (approved 28 January 2025) named 29 January 2025 for Schedule 1, ss. 1-16 (ss. 17 and 18, commencement and short title, are omitted from the consolidation as spent), and named 29 January 2025 and 1 July 2025 for the parts of Schedule 2. Both dates are before today (14 October 2026), so every provision is in force. e-Laws (currency date 9 October 2026) shows the current version from 29 January 2025 and 'No amendments'. The AI duties in ss. 5 and 6 bite only on entities prescribed by regulation, and the only regulations listed are O. Reg. 51/26 (cyber security) and O. Reg. 52/26 (under-18 digital technology); I chose 'In force' rather than 'Partially in force' because the statute is legally in force in full, and recorded the missing AI regulations in notes.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Clearly in scope and unchanged: Schedule 1 contains a part titled 'Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems' setting AI duties for the Ontario public sector, an AI-specific sub-national law.
